content:
samir: Kicking off AZ3 GPU pool bring-up for eu-west-3 — target = 12x A100(80GB). Window 2024-11-03 10:30-12:30 UTC. Posting initial checklist and run commands here. PR: https://git.redwood/example/infra/az3-gpu-pool :eyes:

infra-bot: Ticket created RED-INF-4521 and linked to deploy pipeline (pipeline #782).

alyssa: Quick q — are we attaching these nodes to the shared VPC or an isolated subnet?

samir: Shared VPC. Using subnet 10.60.0.0/22. Node pool name: nodepool-az3-gpu. IAM role required: redwood-gpu-node (has kms, logging, and attestation perms).

mike: FYI account quota check: we currently have only 8 A100 GPUs available in eu-west-3 (raised a ticket with cloud support, ref CS-9987). If quota not increased by 11:00 UTC we'll proceed with 8 nodes and set reserve = 8; adjust autoscaler.

jordan: Validation commands to run after nodes join — paste into runbook for QA:
```
# check nodes labeled for GPU
kubectl get nodes -l workload=gpupool -o wide

# check nvidia drivers and DCGM
kubectl describe node node-az3-001 | grep -i nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-driver-installer

# simple health probe (runs on node):
./scripts/gpu-healthcheck --node node-az3-001 --timeout 60

# check cloud instance metadata for attached GPUs
gcloud compute instances describe node-az3-001 --project=redwood-prod | jq '.guestAccelerators'
```

samir: Also run a small perf test with our tokenized echo model to validate end-to-end latency and KV cache warmup: `loadtest --model rwd-echo --concurrency 4 --duration 2m`. Keep results in /tmp/az3-loadtest-*.json and upload to the deploy ticket.

alyssa: Noted. Any known driver/firmware caveats for A100s in this region?

mike: Yes — last time we saw a mismatch between Nvidia driver and the host kernel after host image updates (caused partial attach failures and OOMs). Workaround: pin driver package to 525.85 for now, and run `nvidia-smi` smoke check during bootstrap. Known issue entry: "A100 attach flakiness if driver >= 530 on kernel 5.x".

infra-bot: Reminder: Canary config will create 2 nodes, then scale to desired. Canary probes: kubelet ready, nvidia-driver installed, kube-proxy status.

jordan: If we hit quota fallback to 8 GPUs, apply this config: 
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: nodepool-az3-gpu
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 8
  gpuType: a100-80gb
```
Also make sure cost center tags are on the instances: `cost_center: infra-gpu-eu` (billing needs it).

samir: Deployment order for the run: 1) create nodepool + subnet + IAM role 2) boot 2 canary nodes 3) run healthchecks from jordan's snippet 4) run perf smoke 5) scale to target (or fallback) 6) handoff to oncall.

mike: Added cloud cost estimate to the ticket — 12 A100s ~ €18k/month (pre-discount). If we go with 8 it's ~€12k/month. Putting numbers into RED-PSA spreadsheet.

alyssa: I'll update the runbook section "AZ bring-ups -> eu-west-3" with the validation commands and known-issues note (driver pin). Also adding a short troubleshooting checklist for network MTU issues we've seen (jumbo frames misconfig).

ops-oncall: I'll take handoff at 12:00 UTC. Please ping me once the canary passes and perf logs are uploaded. +1 once ready. :thumbsup:

samir: Will ping ops-oncall after canary completes. If cloud quota remains low we'll post a quick rollback plan in the ticket. Thanks team! :rocket:
